units.en: A BSTRACT
units.zh: 摘要

units.en: AI agents hold the potential to revolutionize scientific productivity by automating literature reviews, replicating experiments, analyzing data, and even proposing new directions of inquiry; indeed, there are now many such agents, ranging from general- purpose “deep research” systems to specialized science-specific agents, such as AI Scientist and AIGS. Rigorous evaluation of these agents is critical for progress. Yet existing benchmarks fall short on several fronts: they often (1) lack reproducible agent tools necessary for a controlled comparison of core agentic capabilities; (2) do not account for confounding variables such as model cost and tool access; (3) do not provide standardized interfaces for quick agent prototyping and evaluation; (4) fail to provide holistic, product-informed measures of real-world use cases such as science research; and (5) lack comprehensive baseline agents necessary to identify true advances. In response, we define principles and tooling for more rigorously benchmarking agents. Using these, we present AstaBench, a suite that provides a holistic measure of agentic ability to perform scientific research, comprising 2400+ problems spanning the entire scientific discovery process and multiple scientific domains, and including many problems inspired by actual user requests to deployed Asta agents. Our suite comes with the first scientific research environment with production-grade search tools that enable controlled, reproducible evaluation, better accounting for confounders. Alongside, we provide a comprehensive suite of nine science-optimized classes of Asta agents and numerous baselines. Our extensive evaluation of 57 agents across 22 agent classes reveals several interesting findings, most importantly that despite meaningful progress on certain individual aspects, AI remains far from solving the challenge of science research assistance.

units.zh: AI 智能体有望通过自动完成文献综述、复现实验、分析数据，甚至提出新的研究方向，显著改变科研生产率。如今已有众多此类智能体，从通用“深度研究”系统到 AI Scientist、AIGS 等专门科研智能体。严格评价这些智能体对于推动进展至关重要。然而，现有基准存在多方面不足：它们往往（1）缺少对核心智能体能力进行受控比较所必需的可复现工具；（2）没有考虑模型成本、工具访问权限等混杂因素；（3）没有提供用于快速构建和评价智能体的标准接口；（4）未能全面衡量科研等真实使用场景中由产品需求驱动的任务；（5）缺少足够全面的基线来识别真正进步。为此，我们提出更严格的智能体评测原则及工具，并据此构建 AstaBench。该套件全面衡量智能体开展科学研究的能力，包含覆盖整个科学发现过程和多个科学领域的 2,400 余个问题，其中许多问题受到已部署 Asta 智能体真实用户需求的启发。套件提供首个配备生产级检索工具的科学研究环境，支持受控、可复现的评价，并更好地处理混杂因素。此外，我们提供九类面向科学任务优化的 Asta 智能体及众多基线。对 22 类智能体中的 57 个具体智能体开展的广泛评价揭示了若干发现：尤其是，尽管在某些单项能力上已有实质性进展，AI 距离解决科研辅助挑战仍有较大距离。

units.en: 1 I NTRODUCTION
units.zh: 1 引言

units.en: AI agents are increasingly being applied to complex real-world use cases. In particular, they hold the promise to revolutionize scientific productivity by automating reviews of the literature, replicating complex experiments, analyzing high volumes of data, and even proposing new avenues to explore.

units.en: Large organizations such as OpenAI and Google are investing in general-purpose “deep research” systems to help everyone, including scientists, comb through literature much more effectively. We even have specialized science-specific agents, such as AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024; Yamada et al., 2025) and AIGS (Liu et al., 2024), targeting scientific research. With so many different agents—many behind paywalls and all evaluated in bespoke ways—how are end users and AI developers to know which perform best? Unfortunately, existing agent benchmark suites have several deficiencies, when considered as a general measure of AI skill, including for their ability to do scientific research (Table 1). First, suites often lack the standard task environments and tools necessary for realistic, controlled comparison of agents on a level playing field; for example, no large-scale, controlled document retrieval tools exist, making it unclear whether a ‘winning’ agent has superior AI capabilities or merely access to a more relevant information source. Second, they fail to properly account for confounding variables; we are unaware of agent benchmarks that account for variations in tool usage, and only a few like HAL (Kapoor et al., 2025) measure cost, which is critical since even simplistic strategies (e.g., taking a majority vote over repeated invocation) can boost accuracy by spending more (Kapoor et al., 2024). Third, benchmark suite interfaces are rarely standardized for use by general agents, since suite developers typically assume either that users will evaluate only agents that come with the suite (and so it is fine for evals to be coupled to agents, as in the case of OpenHands (Wang et al., 2025) or AutoGen (Fourney et al., 2024)) or that users will build only specialized agents for specific benchmarks (as is the case with general suites like HAL (Kapoor et al., 2025)). Measuring new agents on a full suite typically requires time-consuming interventions ranging from extensive decoupling to manually clarifying task instructions that were not written with general agents in mind; this harms reproducibility and controlled comparison. Fourth, they often lack tasks that are informed by authentic product usage data (typically guarded by technology companies), raising concerns that higher scores may not lead to meaningful real-world benefit. Finally, benchmark suites lack comprehensive agent baselines for proper comparison. As a result, most published evaluations only compare to a small number of other agents or ablations, making it difficult to assess whether claimed improvements represent genuine advances. In response, we present a set of benchmarking principles and a benchmark suite, built upon these principles, that overcomes the aforementioned limitations, along with open-source resources that enable more rigorous, comprehensive measurement. Specifically:

units.zh:
像 OpenAI 和 Google 这样的大型机构正在投资通用“深度研究”系统，以帮助包括科学家在内的所有人更高效地筛选文献。我们甚至还有针对特定科学领域的智能体，例如 AI Scientist（Lu 等，2024；Yamada 等，2025）和 AIGS（Liu 等，2024），它们专注于科学研究领域。由于存在大量不同的智能体——许多受付费限制且均以定制化方式进行评估——最终用户和 AI 开发者如何判断哪些智能体表现最佳呢？不幸的是，现有的智能体基准测试套件在作为衡量 AI 能力的通用指标时存在诸多缺陷，尤其是其在进行科学研究方面的能力（表1）。
首先，这些套件通常缺乏必要的标准任务环境与工具，无法在公平的竞争环境中对智能体进行真实、可控的对比；例如，不存在大规模、可控的文档检索工具，因此难以判断“获胜”的智能体是具备更出色的人工智能能力，还是仅仅拥有更相关的信息来源。
其次，它们未能正确考虑混杂变量；我们并不了解那些能考虑工具使用差异的智能体评估基准，仅有少数研究如 HAL（Kapoor 等，2025）才涉及成本因素，而这一点至关重要，因为即便是简单的策略（例如通过重复调用进行多数投票）也会因增加成本而提升准确率（Kapoor 等，2024）。
第三，通用智能体使用的基准测试套件接口很少实现标准化，因为套件开发者通常认为用户只会评估包含在该套件中的智能体（因此将评估与智能体结合使用是可行的，如 OpenHands (Wang et al., 2025) 或 AutoGen (Fourney et al., 2024) 所示）；或者用户只会为特定基准测试构建专用智能体（就像 HAL (Kapoor et al., 2025) 这类通用套件那样）。
对全新智能体进行全面评估通常需要耗时的操作，包括复杂的分离处理，以及手动明确那些并非为通用智能体设计的任务说明；这会损害可重复性及可控性比较。此外，这些智能体往往缺乏基于真实产品使用数据（通常由技术公司保护）的任务设置，从而让人担心较高的得分可能无法带来实际的实际效益。最后，相关基准测试套件缺乏用于正确比较的完整智能体基线数据。
因此，大多数已发表的评估仅与其他少数智能体或改进方案进行比较，难以判断所声称的改进是否真正具有实质性进展。为应对此问题，我们提出了一套基准测试原则及基于这些原则的基准测试套件，以克服上述限制，同时提供开源资源，从而实现更严格、全面的评估。具体内容包括：

units.en: • We formalize principles for rigorously benchmarking agents (Appendix A), which address key limitations of current agent benchmark suites. • Guided by our principles, we present AstaBench1 (Section 3), a more rigorous agent benchmark suite that is a holistic measure of scientific research, which exercises a broad spectrum of skills— including literature understanding, data understanding, planning, tool use, coding, and search—and comprises over 2400 problems spanning the full scientific discovery process and multiple scientific domains, including many problems based on real user requests from Asta,2 where we have deployed several of our agents for public use. It is easy to integrate new general agents with AstaBench, which provides a standardized task interface. • AstaBench includes the powerful Asta Environment (Section 4), the first agent environment that enables controlled, reproducible evaluation with production-grade search tools for retrieving information from a large corpus of scientific literature. • We also introduce the agent-eval Agents Evaluation Toolkit3 (Section 4.2), which enables defining a benchmark suite and leaderboard with time-invariant cost accounting using model usages logged by Inspect (UK AI Security Institute, 2024), a standard agent evaluation framework that provides broad model and evaluation compatibility. • We introduce AstaBench Leaderboard4 built using this Toolkit. It’s the first agent leaderboard to properly account for confounding variables such as the tools used by the agent and inference cost.

It is easy to integrate new general agents with AstaBench, which provides a standardized task interface. • AstaBench includes the powerful Asta Environment (Section 4), the first agent environment that enables controlled, reproducible evaluation with production-grade search tools for retrieving information from a large corpus of scientific literature. • We also introduce the agent-eval Agents Evaluation Toolkit3 (Section 4.2), which enables defining a benchmark suite and leaderboard with time-invariant cost accounting using model usages logged by Inspect (UK AI Security Institute, 2024), a standard agent evaluation framework that provides broad model and evaluation compatibility. • We

units.zh:
• 我们制定了用于严格评估智能体性能的准则（附录A），这些准则能够解决当前智能体评估体系存在的关键缺陷。• 依据这些准则，我们推出了 AstaBench1（第3节），这是一个更为严谨的智能体评估体系，能够全面衡量科学研究水平，涵盖多种技能——包括文献理解、数据理解、规划、工具使用、编程和搜索等——该体系包含超过2400个问题，覆盖完整的科学发现过程及多个科学领域，其中许多问题基于 Asta 提供的真实用户需求，我们已部署了若干智能体供公众使用。
很容易将新的通用智能体与 AstaBench 集成，后者提供了标准化的任务接口。• AstaBench 包含强大的 Asta 环境（第 4 节），这是首个能够使用生产级搜索工具对大量科学文献进行可控且可复现评估的智能体环境。• 我们还引入了智能体评估工具包 3（第 4.2 节），该工具包能够利用 Inspect（英国人工智能安全研究所，2024）记录到的模型使用数据，通过时间不变的成本核算来定义基准测试套件和排行榜，Inspect 是一种标准的智能体评估框架，具备广泛的模型与评估兼容性。
介绍使用此工具包构建的 AstaBench 排行榜4。这是首个能够充分考虑干扰变量（如智能体使用的工具及推理成本）的智能体排行榜。

units.en: Table 1: AstaBench improves over existing agent benchmark suites in several ways. It tests holistic scientific reasoning (i.e., a broad spectrum of task types and across more than one scientific domain). Many of its problems are inspired by actual user requests to our deployed Asta agents. Its standard tool environment isolates core agentic abilities (e.g., planning, tool-calling, etc.) from information access. AstaBench’s scoring controls for confounders, such as computational cost, and its tasks are defined using a uniform format that supports general-purpose agents. The table’s final column, titled ‘Cls.’, indicates the number of agent classes (e.g., ReAct) that are used to instantiate (e.g., with specific LLMs) the total number of agents listed in preceding column; AstaBench includes more classes of agents than prior benchmarking efforts.

表1：AstaBench在多个方面优于现有的智能体评估基准套件。它测试的是全面的科学推理能力（即涵盖多种任务类型及多个科学领域）。其许多问题都是基于实际用户对部署的Asta智能体的请求而设计的。其标准工具环境将核心智能体功能（如规划、工具调用等）与信息访问分离开来。AstaBench的评分机制能够控制诸如计算成本之类的干扰因素，且其任务采用统一格式定义，可支持通用智能体使用。

units.en: 2 R ELATED W ORK Our efforts relate to two recent threads of research: the development of holistic agent evaluations that test a wide range of LLM-driven automation (for a general review, see Yehudai et al. (2025)) and the development of new benchmarks for measuring the scientific reasoning of LLMs and their use as scientific assistants and agents (Wang et al., 2023). We consider each in turn. Holistic Agent Evaluations The last few years have seen a surge in benchmarks and evaluation frameworks that attempt to holistically measure the reasoning abilities of LLMs (e.g., Gu et al., 2025; Gao et al., 2024; Habib et al., 2023; Guha et al., 2024). Given the rise of LLM-driven automation, recent efforts have centered around new benchmarks and frameworks for evaluating LLM agents. Table 1 highlights recent efforts that are most closely related to AstaBench in terms of their scope as holistic or science agent benchmarks: AutoGenBench (Fourney et al., 2024), BixBench (Mitchener et al., 2025), BrowserGym (Le Sellier De Chezelles et al., 2025), the Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL) (Kapoor et al., 2025), Inspect Evals (UK AI Safety Institute and Arcadia Impact and Vector Institute, 2025), Lab-Bench (Laurent et al., 2024), OpenHands Evals (Wang et al., 2025), ScienceAgentBench (Chen et al., 2025b), Terminal-Bench (The Terminal-Bench Team, 2025a), and the Vector Institute Leaderboard (Vector Institute, 2025).6 We compare these efforts to AstaBench across the following dimensions: holistic scientific reasoning (i.e., focuses on a broad spectrum of task types and across more than one scientific domain), product usage-based (i.e., involves tasks based on product use cases), controlled, realistic tools (i.e., distributes standard, realistic tools that allow for controlled comparison of agents), scoring accounts for confounders (i.e., scores systematically account for cost, controlled tool use, and other confounders), general agents (i.e., tasks have uniform formats that support general-purpose agents), and number of agents (i.e., total number and number of different classes of agent). AstaBench stands out on these dimensions, which are key to advancing scientific AI and increasing benchmarking rigor generally (Appendix A). In terms of science, the other agent benchmark suites are all less holistic, either more limited in terms of task category (e.g., HAL’s only science tasks are coding tasks) or the domain (e.g., LAB-Bench is limited to biology); AstaBench is also the only benchmark to leverage data from a companion product (Asta) in its tasks. Despite its importance, few suites have seriously focused on cost (HAL is an exception), and none have distributed standard tools that are decoupled from agents or agent frameworks. While some leaderboards are scaling up the number of agents they test (again, notably HAL), all test far fewer agent classes (architectures) compared to AstaBench, which also distributes open-source code for these agent classes through agent-baselines Agents Suite. Science Benchmarks and Agents for Science Naturally, the rise of powerful large language models (LLMs) has led to much recent interest in LLM-driven approaches to scientific research-related tasks. Many new benchmarks have been developed, often focusing on particular sub-problems in the full research pipeline, including scientific coding and execution (Tian et al., 2024; Lai et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2025a; Chan et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2024), data analysis (Majumder et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2025), research reproduction (Bogin et al., 2024; Siegel et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2025; Kon et al., 2025; Xiang et al., 2025; Starace et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2025; Yan et al., 2025), ideation and hypothesis generation (Ruan et al., 2024; Si et al., 2024; Vasu et al., 2025), and literature retrieval and understanding (Shi et al., 2025; He et al., 2025), among others (Zhu et al., 2025). AstaBench 6 Agent counts for Table 1 were derived from live leaderboards and repositories accessed August 2025, in addition to the canonical benchmark references (Microsoft, 2024; ServiceNow, 2025; SAgE Team, Princeton University, 2025; ArcadiaImpact / UK Government BEIS Team, 2025; All-Hands-AI, 2025a;b; The Terminal- Bench Team, 2025b).

units.zh:
2 相关工作 我们的研究涉及两个近期的研究方向：一是开发全面智能体评估方法，以测试各种由大语言模型驱动的自动化应用（有关总体综述，请参考 Yehudai 等，2025）；二是开发新的基准测试，用于衡量大语言模型的科学推理能力及其作为科学助手和智能体的应用效果（Wang 等，2023）。我们将依次讨论这两个方向。全面智能体评估 过去几年中，旨在全面评估大语言模型推理能力的基准测试与评估框架数量激增（例如，Gu 等，2025；Gao 等，2024；Habib 等，2023；Guha 等，2024）。
鉴于大语言模型驱动的自动化趋势日益凸显，近期的工作重点集中在用于评估大语言模型智能体的新基准测试与框架上。
表1列出了与AstaBench在整体或科学智能体基准领域最相关的近期研究：AutoGenBench（Fourney等，2024）、BixBench（Mitchener等，2025）、BrowserGym（Le Sellier De Chezelles等，2025）、Holistic Agent Leaderboard（HAL）（Kapoor等，2025）、Inspect Evals（英国人工智能安全研究所、Arcadia Impact及Vector Institute，2025）、Lab-Bench（Laurent等，2024）、OpenHands Evals（Wang等，2025）、ScienceAgentBench（Chen等，2025b）、Terminal-Bench（Terminal-Bench团队，2025a）以及Vector Institute Leaderboard（Vector Institute，2025）。我们针对这些研究与AstaBench进行了比较。
维度包括：整体科学推理（即关注多种任务类型及多个科学领域）；基于产品使用的任务（即涉及基于产品用例的任务）；可控且真实的工具（即提供标准、真实的工具，以便对智能体进行可控比较）；考虑混杂因素的评分标准（即评分系统地考虑了成本、可控工具使用及其他混杂因素）；通用智能体（即任务具有统一格式，支持通用型智能体）；以及智能体的数量（即总数量及不同类别的智能体数量）。
AstaBench在这些方面表现突出，这些特点对于推动科学人工智能的发展以及提升整体基准测试的严谨性至关重要（附录A）。在科学领域方面，其他智能体基准测试套件都缺乏全面性，要么任务类别有限（例如HAL仅包含编程任务），要么领域范围受限（例如LAB-Bench仅限于生物学）；而AstaBench是唯一一个在其任务中利用配套产品Asta数据的基准测试套件。尽管其重要性不言而喻，但很少有套件真正关注成本问题（HAL是个例外），也没有任何套件提供与智能体或智能体框架无关的标准工具。
虽然一些排行榜会增加所测试智能体的数量（同样以 HAL 为例），但所有排行榜所测试的智能体类别数量都远少于 AstaBench，而 AstaBench 还通过 agent-baselines Agents Suite 提供这些智能体类别的开源代码。科学基准与科学智能体 显然，强大的大语言模型的出现使得人们对基于大语言模型的科学研究相关任务方法产生了极大的兴趣。许多新的基准测试也已被开发出来，通常专注于整个研究流程中的特定子问题，包括科学编码与执行（Tian 等，2024；Lai 等，2023；Chen 等，2025a；Chan 等，2025）。

units.en: spans many of these task categories, and provides the most comprehensive evaluation of scientific agent performance to date (Table 1). Increased LLM capabilities have led to emergence of a host of agents for end-to-end, open-ended sci- entific discovery, including AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024; Yamada et al., 2025), Agent Lab (Schmidgall et al., 2025), AIGS (Liu et al., 2024), and CodeScientist (Jansen et al., 2025), among others (Cheng et al., 2025). To bring clarity to this area (and accelerate its progress), AstaBench introduces a new end-to-end task that evaluates an agent’s ability to complete a research project, starting from an idea and ending with a written report and code. We believe this task is a useful complement to the many existing benchmarks that focus on more narrow problems in the research pipeline.

units.en: 3 A STA B ENCH : A H OLISTIC S CIENTIFIC R ESEARCH B ENCHMARK S UITE We present AstaBench, the first benchmark suite for holistic evaluation of agents’ ability to perform scientific research. Crucially, our suite is reproducible even as science progresses, since it comes with the first realistic, reproducible search tools (Section 4). Our suite implements a new standard interface for agent benchmark suites and provides time-invariant cost reporting through the agent-eval Agents Evaluation Toolkit (Section 4.2)). As such, AstaBench is ready for use by new general agents such as those in our agent baselines suite (Section 4.3).

units.zh: 3 ASTA BENCH：全面评估智能体科研能力的基准测试套件 我们推出了 AstaBench，这是首个用于全面评估智能体进行科研能力的标准化基准测试套件。重要的是，即使科学领域不断发展，该套件依然具有可重复性，因为它配备了首个真实的、可复现的检索工具（第4节）。该套件采用了新的智能体基准测试套件接口，并通过智能体评估工具包提供时间不变的成本报告（第4.2节）。因此，AstaBench 已准备好被新的通用智能体使用，例如我们智能体基线套件中的那些智能体（第4.3节）。

units.en: AstaBench comprises the following 11 benchmarks (summarized in Table 2, with full details in Appendix E and example inputs in Appendix H; note that AstaBench uses slightly modified versions of some of the cited datasets): PaperFindingBench tests an agent’s ability to handle challenging scientific search queries. LitQA2-FullText/LitQA2-FullText-Search (Skarlinski et al., 2024) measure an agent’s ability to answer questions and retrieve papers within the biomed- ical domain. ScholarQA-CS2 tests an agent’s ability to answer long-form scientific questions. ArxivDIGESTables-Clean (Newman et al., 2024) tests an agent’s ability to create a literature review table. SUPER-Expert (Bogin et al., 2024) tests the ability of code agents to set up and execute Python machine learning experiments reported in ML and NLP papers. CORE-Bench- Hard− (Siegel et al., 2025) tests an agent’s ability to reproduce experiments and analyses from papers.7 DS-1000 (Lai et al., 2023) tests the ability of agents on data science tasks encountered in research. DiscoveryBench (Majumder et al., 2025) tests whether the agent can automatically find and verify hypotheses from given dataset(s). E2E-Bench/E2E-Bench-Hard test whether agents can perform the full research pipeline of ideation, planning, (software) experiment design, implementation, execution, analysis, and producing a final report. Full details of how these tasks are scored can be found in Appendix E. Some use LLMs as judges to evaluate outputs against rubrics (PaperFindingBench, ScholarQA-CS2, ArxivDIGESTables- Clean, DiscoveryBench, E2E-Bench, E2E-Bench-Hard) while others use programmatic eval- uation (LitQA2-FullText, LitQA2-FullText-Search, SUPER-Expert, CORE-Bench-Hard− , DS-1000).

Some use LLMs as judges to evaluate outputs against rubrics (PaperFindingBench, ScholarQA-CS2, ArxivDIGESTables- Clean, DiscoveryBench, E2E-Bench, E2E-Bench-Hard) while others use programmatic eval- uation (LitQA2-FullText, LitQA2-FullText-Search, SUPER-Expert, CORE-Bench-Hard− , DS-1000).
units.zh:
AstaBench包含以下11个评估基准（详见表2，完整细节见附录E，示例输入见附录H；注意AstaBench使用了部分引用数据集的稍作修改版本）：PaperFindingBench用于测试智能体处理具有挑战性的科学搜索查询的能力。LitQA2-FullText/LitQA2-FullText-Search（Skarlinski等，2024）用于衡量智能体回答问题及在生物医学领域检索论文的能力。ScholarQA-CS2用于测试智能体回答长篇科学问题的能力。ArxivDIGESTables-Clean（Newman等，2024）用于测试智能体生成文献综述表格的能力。
SUPER-Expert（Bogin等，2024）测试了代码智能体设置并执行ML与NLP论文中所述的Python机器学习实验的能力。CORE-Bench-Hard-（Siegel等，2025）测试了智能体复现论文中的实验与分析的能力。DS-1000（Lai等，2023）测试了智能体在研究中所涉及的数据科学任务中的能力。DiscoveryBench（Majumder等，2025）则测试了智能体能否从给定数据集中自动发现并验证假设。
E2E-Bench/E2E-Bench-Hard 的测试旨在检验智能体能否完成从构思、规划、（软件）实验设计、实现、执行、分析到最终报告生成的完整研究流程。关于这些任务评分方式的详细内容可参见附录E。部分测试使用大语言模型作为评判者，根据评分标准对输出结果进行评估（如 PaperFindingBench、ScholarQA-CS2、ArxivDIGESTables-Clean、DiscoveryBench、E2E-Bench、E2E-Bench-Hard），而另一些则采用程序化评估方式（如 LitQA2-FullText、LitQA2-FullText-Search、SUPER-Expert、CORE-Bench-Hard、DS-1000）。

It provides the following specific tools via the MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard: snippet_search, search_papers_by_relevance, get_paper, get_paper_batch, get_- citations, search_authors_by_name, get_author_papers, search_paper_by_title Computational Notebook: A stateful computational (Jupyter) notebook. The tool can execute Python code as well as standard IPython magic commands like %%writefile, %matplotlib inline, and !shell_command. Python variables and environment are maintained between calls so that the tool can be used to solve problems incrementally. By default, the tool returns a timeout message to the agent if a single cell takes more than 5 minutes to execute. Since the tool needs to execute code, it lives in a new sandbox image that’s created by the framework. Our tools feature improved agent compatibility compared to other suites. They are cleanly decoupled from agents and provide easy integration via MCP. Code executed in our sandbox can call tools provided by the main (host) execution environment (e.g., Asta Scientific Corpus), enabling testing of code execution agents, e.g., agents that implement the CodeAct (Wang et al., 2024) pattern.

关于这些论文的机制（适用于详细的文献分析，例如在 ArxivDIGESTables- Clean 中）。它通过 MCP（模型上下文协议）标准提供以下特定工具：snippet_search、search_papers_by_relevance、get_paper、get_paper_batch、get_citations、search_authors_by_name、get_author_papers、search_paper_by_title。计算笔记本：一个状态化的计算型（Jupyter）笔记本。该工具可以执行 Python 代码以及标准的 IPython magic 命令，如 %%writefile、%matplotlib inline 和!shell_command。Python 变量和环境在调用之间得以保持，因此该工具可用于逐步解决问题。
默认情况下，如果单个单元格的执行时间超过5分钟，该工具会向智能体返回超时消息。由于该工具需要执行代码，它运行在由框架生成的新沙箱镜像中。与其他套件相比，我们的工具具有更好的智能体兼容性。它们与智能体完全解耦，并通过MCP实现轻松集成。在我们的沙箱中执行的代码可以调用主执行环境提供的工具（例如Asta Scientific Corpus），从而能够测试代码执行智能体，例如实现CodeAct（Wang等人，2024）模式的智能体。

units.en: We use Inspect (UK AI Security Institute, 2024) as the framework for implementing our individual agentic benchmarks, as it provides broad model provider and tool compatibility, useful logging and debugging affordances, and a growing set of compatible evals (UK AI Safety Institute and Arcadia Impact and Vector Institute, 2025). However, Inspect logs only model usages (not normalized dollar amounts) and it lacks tooling for defining benchmark suites with unified scoring or leaderboards. To fill this gap, we present the agent-eval8 agent leaderboard toolkit, which provides a benchmark suite, reporting, and leaderboard layer on top of a suite of Inspect-formatted benchmarks; it features: Time-invariant cost calculation: The agent-eval toolkit computes normalized dollar costs based on model usages logged through Inspect. For mapping model usages to prices, we use a frozen snapshot of the litellm cost map, which is community-sourced for broad model coverage.9 It factors in cache discounts for agents that take advantage of caching, as this is an increasingly adopted optimization technique (and providers like OpenAI provide these discounts automatically); however, 8 https://github.com/allenai/agent-eval 9 We supplement the cost map with prices for custom models based on Together AI (https://www.toge ther.ai/) generic model size-based pricing.

units.zh:
我们采用 Inspect（英国人工智能安全研究所，2024）作为实施个人智能体基准测试的框架，因为它具备广泛的模型提供方与工具兼容性、实用的日志记录与调试功能，以及不断增加的兼容评估方案（英国人工智能安全研究所、Arcadia Impact及Vector Institute，2025）。然而，Inspect 的日志仅记录模型使用情况（而非标准化金额），且缺乏用于定义具有统一评分或排行榜的基准测试套件的工具。
为了填补这一空白，我们推出了 agent-eval8 智能体排行榜工具包，该工具包在一系列 Inspect 格式基准测试之上提供了评估套件、报告功能以及排行榜模块；其特点包括：时间不变的成本计算：agent-eval 工具包根据通过 Inspect 记录的模型使用情况来计算标准化美元成本。
为了将模型使用情况与价格进行对应，我们使用了 Litellm 成本图的冻结快照，该快照由社区共同生成，能够覆盖多种模型。该模型考虑了利用缓存的智能体所享受到的缓存折扣，因为这是一种越来越被采用的优化技术（如 OpenAI 等提供商会自动提供这些折扣）；然而，我们还根据 Together AI (ther.ai/) 通用的模型规模定价方式，为定制模型补充了价格信息。

units.en: 5 E XPERIMENTS
units.zh: 5 项实验

units.en: We now present experimental results, which we have also used to seed the interactive AstaBench leaderboard.14 Our experiments were conducted over a period of several months. Since one may boost scores by using more compute (eg using repetition and majority vote) (Dodge et al., 2019), we report cost as well as accuracy. We also report the standard deviation of our measurements. For brevity, when an agent was tested with multiple different models, we report the top result(s) plus any other significant data points. The entire set of results, plus plots of scores vs. costs including the Pareto frontier (showing the best agent for a given cost), are in Appendix D. Some agents (e.g., ReAct) can attempt all 11 benchmarks; others are category-specific or even benchmark-specific. Table 4 shows the overall results for those agents attempting all benchmarks, as well as agents that can solve all the benchmarks in at least one category. Category- and benchmark- specific results are presented in Appendix C for space reasons. As noted above, agents powered by closed weight LLMs currently far exceed the reach of those powered by open weight LLMs. On the other hand, simply switching the underlying LLM with the latest and greatest one isn’t necessarily a reliable recipe for success on AstaBench. As a case in point, one of the newest LLMs, gpt-5, provides only a modest boost over an earlier “reasoning LLM”, o3, except on three benchmarks. In fact, gpt-5 hurts the performance of several specialized agents. Tools designed specifically for science research assistance can significantly help AI agents. This is most noticable with Asta v0, which scores ∼9% higher than the next best agent, ReAct with gpt-5 (53.0% vs. 44.0%). However, this comes with the trade-off of significantly higher development (engineering) cost, and (for some tasks, specifically in end-to-end-discovery) higher inference cost. None of the commercial scientific research agents were able to perform the full range of research tasks in AstaBench. The entire set of results, plus plots of scores vs. costs including the Pareto frontier (showing the best agent for a given cost), are in Appendix D.

Some agents (e.g., ReAct) can attempt all 11 benchmarks; others are category-specific or even benchmark-specific. Table 4 shows the overall results for those agents attempting all benchmarks, as well as agents that can solve all the benchmarks in at least one category. Category- and benchmark- specific results are presented in Appendix C for space reasons. As noted above, agents powered by closed weight LLMs currently far exceed the reach of those powered by open weight LLMs. On the other hand, simply switching the underlying LLM with the latest and greatest one isn’t necessarily a reliable recipe for success on AstaBench.

As a case in point, one of the newest LLMs, gpt-5, provides only a modest boost over an earlier “reasoning LLM”, o3, except on three benchmarks. In fact, gpt-5 hurts the performance of several specialized agents. Tools designed specifically for science research assistance can significantly help AI agents. This is most noticable with Asta v0, which scores ∼9% higher than the next best agent, ReAct with gpt-5 (53.0% vs. 44.0%). However, this comes with the trade-off of significantly higher development (engineering) cost, and (for some tasks, specifically in end-to-end-discovery) higher inference cost.

None of the commercial scientific research agents were able to perform the full range of research tasks in AstaBench. units.en: one (OpenAI Deep Research) score well on literature understanding, but are unable to perform the full spectrum of science research assistance. Science research assistance is still far from solved, as evidenced by the generally low overall scores for the full gamut of agents, from fully open to fully closed. For example: The best open source agent with open weights LLMs scores a terrible 11.1% (Smolagents Coder with Llama-4-Scout-17B- 16E-Instruct) (Table 4). The best open source agent with closed LLM(s) is much better: 53.0% (Asta v0) (Table 4). While the best API-based agent (FutureHouse Falcon) and closed agent (OpenAI Deep Research) score well on a single benchmark (Table 6), they are stymied by the full range of tasks. The cost-performance tradeoff across agents, highlighted by the Asta leaderboard’s Pareto curve provides several interesting insights. The best economical model is ReAct with gpt-5-mini, scoring 32%—within 21% (absolute) of the best performing models—while costing over an order of magnitude less at $0.04 per problem. Powering a general agent with an expensive model can lower the overall cost. Though the per-token cost is 3 to 25 times lower for gemini-flash and llama-scout compared to o3 or sonnet, the weaker models often take more steps or get stuck in loops, causing a ReAct agent to end up being twice as expensive in addition to lower-performing. Surprisingly, most of our specialized agents (Asta Scholar QA (Table 6), Asta DataVoyager (Table 4), Asta Code (Table 8)) perform worse with gpt-5 than with previous models, while ReAct performs much better. One possible explanation for this is that gpt-5 has been tuned to do well with now-common ReAct-style workflows, and conversely may be relatively less adaptive to alternate workflows. If this is indeed true, and trends continue, there may be diminishing value in application-specific workflows. As the LLM underlying ReAct, gpt-5’s boost over o3 is generally light, with only a gain of 0%- 5% across most benchmarks. However, gpt-5 provides a huge boost in 4 benchmarks: +13.4% absolute on ScholarQA-CS2 (Table 6), + 24.8% on SUPER-Expert (Table 8), +25.3% on LitQA2- FullText-Search (Table 5), and +21.1% on E2E-Bench-Hard (Table 10). In general, today’s agents are reasonably good at literature understanding. However, despite some recent progress, coding, experiment execution, data analysis, and data-driven discovery still remain major, unsolved problems for science assistance agents. Literature Understanding: For literature search agents, Asta Paper Finder stands out as an impressive system, scoring much higher than its closest rival (ReAct) on PaperFindingBench and LitQA2-FullText-Search (Table 5). Despite this, it is clear that the paper-finding task is far from ‘solved,’ requiring further work to achieve truly comprehensive results. For literature question-answering agents, our results (Table 6) suggest that (among other things): The best models have relatively good performance in this category, scoring around 80%. This is likely because literature understanding has been a strong focus of many task-optimized agents in the community (or conversely, the community has targeted literature understanding because this category is particularly well suited for language models). Asta Scholar QA, Elicit, and SciSpace Deep Review are the best tools on these tests (all score about 85% or higher on ScholarQA-CS2, Table 6). For all three tools, the higher performance is driven by the citation subscores of the evaluation. The other external/commercial agents are not far behind, but also do not do significantly better than the best ReAct baseline. This is indeed surprising given ReAct’s simplicity, but is also an indicator of the challenging nature of the task that requires system responses to be precise and cover the relevant points as well as cite the correct supporting sources for claims as necessary. For literature review table generation agents, our results (Table 7) suggest that: even the best models do not yet achieve strong performance in this category, with recall scores around 43%, likely due to limited efforts to build task-optimized agents in this space. Asta Table Synthesis, backed by gpt-5, wins on this task, beating the best general agents. However, Asta Table Synthesis backed by gpt-5-mini also shows competitive performance, at just 13% of the cost. This is indeed surprising given ReAct’s simplicity, but is also an indicator of the challenging nature of the task that requires system responses to be precise and cover the relevant points as well as cite the correct supporting sources for claims as necessary. For literature review table generation agents, our results (Table 7) suggest that: even the best models do not yet achieve strong performance in this category, with recall scores around 43%, likely due to limited efforts to build task-optimized agents in this space.

Asta Table Synthesis, backed by gpt-5, wins on this task, beating the best general agents. However, Asta Table Synthesis backed by gpt-5-mini also shows competitive performance, at just 13% of the cost. 其中一个（OpenAI Deep Research）在大语言模型文献理解方面表现良好，但无法提供全面的科学研究辅助服务。由于从完全开放到完全封闭的各种智能体整体得分普遍较低，科学研究辅助问题仍远未解决。例如：最佳开源智能体使用开放权重的大语言模型得分仅为11.1%（Smolagents Coder with Llama-4-Scout-17B- 16E-Instruct）（表4）。而最佳开源智能体使用封闭大语言模型则表现更好：得分为53.0%（Asta v0）（表4）。
虽然最佳的基于 API 的智能体（FutureHouse Falcon）和封闭型智能体（OpenAI Deep Research）在单一基准测试中的得分很高（见表 6），但在各种任务中却存在局限。Asta 排行榜的帕累托曲线揭示了不同智能体在成本与性能之间的权衡关系，提供了许多有价值的见解。最经济高效的模型是使用 gpt-5-mini 的 ReAct 模型，其得分为 32%，比表现最好的模型高出 21%（绝对值），而每个问题的成本则低了约一个数量级，仅为 0.04 美元。使用昂贵的模型来驱动通用智能体反而可能降低整体成本。
尽管与 o3 或 sonnet 相比，Gemini-Flash 和 Llama-Scout 的每个标记成本低 3 到 25 倍，但较弱的模型往往需要更多步骤或陷入循环，导致 ReAct 智能体不仅成本更高，性能也较差。令人惊讶的是，我们大多数专用智能体（Asta Scholar QA（表 6）、Asta DataVoyager（表 4）、Asta Code（表 8））在使用 GPT-5 时的表现不如使用之前版本的模型，而 ReAct 则表现得更好。对此的一种可能解释是，GPT-5 经过调整，能够很好地适应当前常见的 ReAct 风格工作流，而相比之下可能对其他工作流适应性较低。
如果这一情况确实如此，且趋势持续下去，特定应用场景中的工作流程可能会逐渐失去价值。作为 ReAct 背后的大语言模型，gpt-5 相对于 o3 的提升幅度通常较小，大多数基准测试中的提升仅达到 0% 至 5%。然而，gpt-5 在四个基准测试中取得了显著进步：在 ScholarQA-CS2 上绝对提升 13.4%（表 6），在 SUPER-Expert 上提升 24.8%（表 8），在 LitQA2- FullText-Search 上提升 25.3%（表 5），在 E2E-Bench-Hard 上提升 21.1%（表 10）。总体而言，如今的智能体在文献理解方面已经相当出色。
然而，尽管近期取得了一些进展，编程、实验执行、数据分析以及数据驱动发现仍是大语言模型科学辅助智能体面临的主要未解决问题。文献理解方面：对于文献搜索智能体而言，Asta Paper Finder是一个出色的系统，在PaperFindingBench和LitQA2-FullText-Search测试集上的得分远高于其最接近的竞争对手ReAct（见表5）。尽管如此，很明显文献查找任务远未“解决”，还需要进一步研究才能取得真正全面的结果。
对于文献问答智能体而言，我们的结果（表6）表明：（除其他因素外）：最佳模型在该类别中的表现相对较好，得分约为80%。这很可能是因为许多针对特定任务的智能体一直将文献理解作为重点研究领域（或者相反，社区也专注于文献理解，因为该类别特别适合语言模型）。Asta Scholar QA、Elicit 和 SciSpace Deep Review是这些测试中的最佳工具（在ScholarQA-CS2上均获得约85%或更高的分数，见表6）。对于这三种工具而言，较高的表现源于评估中的引用子分数。
其他外部/商业智能体也并不落后，但表现也未能显著优于最佳的 ReAct 基准模型。考虑到 ReAct 的简洁性，这一结果确实令人惊讶，同时也表明该任务具有挑战性——系统响应需要精确且涵盖相关要点，同时必要时还需引用正确的支持来源来支撑主张。对于文献综述表格生成智能体而言，我们的结果（表7）表明：即便是最优秀的模型，在这一类别中也尚未达到优异水平，召回率约为43%，这很可能是因为在该领域构建针对任务优化的智能体的努力有限。
由 GPT-5 支持的 Asta Table Synthesis 在这项任务中获胜，超越了最优秀的通用智能体。然而，由 GPT-5-mini 支持的 Asta Table Synthesis 也表现出具有竞争力的性能，其成本仅为后者的 13%。代码与执行：代码与执行问题远未解决——所有智能体在这项任务中的得分都较低，例如，除两个外，所有智能体的 SUPER-Expert 得分均低于 25%，而使用 GPT-5 的 ReAct 方式则得分为 41%

We see agents struggle with this benchmark, with the maximum score being only 34% (Table 4) despite increased attention in the community. End-to-End Discovery: End-to-end discovery remains far from being meaningfully solved. Although the average research step completion scores appear reasonable (scores up to ∼70%, Table 10), the likelihood of completing all experiment steps remains near zero. For example, given ∼10 steps per experiment, and a success rate of 70% per step, the success rate to complete all steps in the experiment will be ≈ 0.710 ≈ 3% (see Table 20 for actual numbers, reaching a maximum of 5%). A lot more work is needed, and we hope these benchmarks will help push research forward in this direction.

还需要更多的工作，我们希望这些基准测试能有助于推动相关研究向这个方向发展。

units.zh: 6 结论与未来工作

units.en: In summary, we identify limitations of current approaches to benchmarking agents, and present methodology and tooling for doing so more rigorously. Using this methodology and tooling, we introduce AstaBench, a holistic benchmark suite for scientific research that addresses key limitations. AstaBench is the first major agent benchmark suite to come with standard environment and tools that enable controlled comparison of agents: the Asta Environment, the first scientific research environment for agents with realistic, controlled search tools. Alongside, we present the agent- baselines Agents Suite, a large suite of standardized agents, which we used to conduct experiments on AstaBench with 57 agents across 22 architectural classes. This revealed several interesting findings, most importantly that despite meaningful progress on certain individual aspects, agentic AI remains far from solving the challenge of scientific research assistance. We invite the community to make submissions to the AstaBench Leaderboard, which is powered by our agent-eval Agents Evaluation Toolkit. This work opens up many exciting possibilities for the agentic AI, scientific research assistance, and automated scientific discovery communities. We are actively pushing the performance-cost frontiers in AstaBench and closing the gap for truly open agents by developing new agent techniques, tools, and open models specialized for scientific research. We are also enhancing agent abilities to manage complex context, from improving on Asta v0 simple orchestration techniques to handling long-duration tasks in complex research projects. We are continuing to research how to refine our LLM-as-a-judge grading procedures, especially for challenging scientific discovery tasks. We plan to develop fresh benchmark problems that use the latest scientific knowledge, which is contamination- resistant and past the training cut-off date of models. We also plan to build benchmarks that test more aspects of collaboration with humans, and deepen coverage of problems in impactful fields such as biomedicine. Finally, we are committed to continuing to measure the latest advances—both by testing the latest LLMs and by adding more agent architectures to agent-baselines.

总结来说，我们指出了当前智能体基准测试方法的局限性，并提出了更严谨的实施方法和工具。通过这些方法和工具，我们推出了 AstaBench——一套用于科学研究的全面基准测试套件，能够解决关键问题。AstaBench是首个包含标准环境与工具的智能体基准测试套件，可帮助进行可控的智能体比较：包括 Asta 环境，这是首个具备真实、可控搜索工具的智能体科研环境。
同时，我们还推出了基于智能体的基准测试套件——Agents Suite，这是一个标准化的智能体集合工具。我们利用该套件在 AstaBench 上进行了实验，共使用了 57 个智能体，涵盖 22 种架构类型。实验结果揭示了一些有趣的发现，最重要的是，尽管在某些具体方面取得了显著进展，但智能体人工智能仍远未能解决科研辅助的挑战。我们邀请社区成员向由我们的智能体评估工具包支持的 AstaBench 排行榜提交作品。这项工作为智能体人工智能、科研辅助以及自动化科学发现领域带来了许多令人兴奋的机遇。
我们正在积极推动 AstaBench 中的性能与成本边界突破，通过开发适用于科学研究的新型智能体技术、工具及开放模型，缩小真正开放智能体的差距。我们还提升了智能体处理复杂上下文的能力，从改进 Asta v0 的简单调度技术到应对复杂研究项目中的长期任务。我们继续研究如何优化我们的 LLM作为评判者的评分流程，尤其是针对具有挑战性的科学发现任务。我们计划开发基于最新科学知识的全新基准问题，这些问题能够抵抗污染并超出模型的训练截止日期。
我们还计划构建测试人类协作多种方面的基准测试，并扩大在生物医学等具有影响力的领域中的问题覆盖范围。最后，我们致力于持续衡量最新进展——既通过测试最新的大语言模型，也通过向基于智能体的基线模型中添加更多智能体架构来实现。

units.en: We took care to adhere to a high ethics bar. We obtained legal review for all material presented in this work. The new real-world user queries used in the Literature Understanding tasks were collected with user consent. We also credit any benchmarks that we adapted for use in our suite, as well as agents that we leverage, citing those works. When measuring existing agents, we worked with the agent creators where possible to ensure they are measured fairly, including Elicit, Future House, and SciSpace.

units.en: We took special care to make this work reproducible; indeed, reproducibility is a core value proposi- tion of our benchmark suite. AstaBench comes with open source code for all included benchmarks, agents, and core infrastructure—as well as logs of all reported experiment. The framework logs and reports specific repository commits, including for data. The agent tools in AstaBench improve reproducibility by providing date-restricted access to the supporting document corpus.

units.zh: 我们特别注重确保该过程的可复现性；实际上，可复现性正是我们基准测试套件的核心价值主张。AstaBench 提供了所有包含的基准测试、智能体及核心基础设施的开源代码，以及所有实验报告的日志。该框架还会记录特定仓库的提交信息，包括数据相关的提交。AstaBench 中的智能体工具通过提供对相关文档语料的限制日期访问权限，从而提升可复现性。

units.zh: 如果没有一个广泛且支持性的社区，这项工作就不可能完成。尤其要感谢：David Albright和Kyle Wiggers在沟通支持与有益反馈方面所做的贡献；Crystal Nam在法律支持上的帮助；Ali Farhadi和Sophie Lebrecht在富有洞察力的反馈与鼓励方面的支持；Stephen Kelman在设计支持上的协助；Inspect评估框架的创建者与维护者；我们所整合的外部数据集的创建者；以及为这些数据集及我们创建的数据集的构建做出贡献的数据工作者们。

units.en: A P RINCIPLES FOR B ENCHMARKING AGENTS
pieces: A P RINCIPLES FOR B ENCHMARKING AGENTS
units.zh: 大语言模型智能体评估的若干原则

units.en: We propose the following principles for more rigorously benchmarking agents:
pieces: We propose the following principles for more rigorously benchmarking agents:
units.zh: 我们提出以下原则，以更严格地对智能体进行基准测试：

units.en: 1. The task suite must represent the complexity of real-world usage. In order to determine whether agents can serve as effective assistants for a use case, it is necessary to test a broad range of relevant tasks. Real-world product usage provides an informative basis for determining appropriate tasks, but unfortunately such data is typically guarded by product companies (who use it to create private evaluations) and unavailable to academic benchmark creators. Moreover, in order to measure progress towards broadly capable agents, the task suite should require exercising a range of advanced, general skills such as reasoning, planning, tool use, search, coding, and data analysis. 2. A standard, realistic, and reproducible environment and tools must accompany the suite for controlled comparison of AI capabilities. The environment should be realistic to measure agents’ ability to act in the real world. At the same time, the environment and tools must be standard and reproducible to facilitate controlled comparison across different agents. Most existing benchmark suites lack standard tools, leading agent developers to use disparate environments and tools that obscure whether performance differences are due to superior AI capabilities or other enhancements. It is particularly important that benchmark suites provide standard search tools with reproducible test-time access to the same document corpus, yet large-scale, optimized search indexes are costly to create and public search tools are not reproducible; we are unaware of any such public, reproducible, large-scale search tools. 3. Reporting must account for confounding variables—especially computational cost and tool usage. It’s essential to account for cost, since even simplistic strategies, such as repeating a task many times and taking majority votes, can boost accuracy by burning cash Kapoor et al. (2024; 2025). Controlling for tool usage is also essential to separate gains due to model or agent architecture advancements from benefits due to privileged access to specialized information sources.

In order to determine whether agents can serve as effective assistants for a use case, it is necessary to test a broad range of relevant tasks. Real-world product usage provides an informative basis for determining appropriate tasks, but unfortunately such data is typically guarded by product companies (who use it to create private evaluations) and unavailable to academic benchmark creators. Moreover, in order to measure progress towards broadly capable agents, the task suite should require exercising a range of advanced, general skills such as reasoning, planning, tool use, search, coding, and data analysis. 2.

A standard, realistic, and reproducible environment and tools must accompany the suite for controlled comparison of AI capabilities. The environment should be realistic to measure agents’ ability to act in the real world. At the same time, the environment and tools must be standard and reproducible to facilitate controlled comparison across different agents. Most existing benchmark suites lack standard tools, leading agent developers to use disparate environments and tools that obscure whether performance differences are due to superior AI capabilities or other enhancements.

It is particularly important that benchmark suites provide standard search tools with reproducible test-time access to the same document corpus, yet large-scale, optimized search indexes are costly to create and public search tools are not reproducible; we are unaware of any such public, reproducible, large-scale search tools. 3. Reporting must account for confounding variables—especially computational cost and tool usage. It’s essential to account for cost, since even simplistic strategies, such as repeating a task many times and taking majority votes, can boost accuracy by burning cash Kapoor et al. (2024; 2025).
Controlling for tool usage is also essential to separate gains due to model or agent architecture advancements from benefits due to privileged access to specialized information sources.
units.zh:
1. 任务集必须能够反映现实世界中的使用复杂性。为了判断智能体能否成为特定用例的有效助手，有必要测试多种相关任务。现实世界的产品使用为确定合适的任务提供了依据，但遗憾的是，此类数据通常由产品公司掌控（他们利用这些数据进行私有评估），无法提供给学术基准创建者使用。此外，为了衡量具备广泛能力的智能体的发展程度，任务集应要求执行一系列高级、通用的技能，如推理、规划、工具使用、搜索、编程和数据分析。  
2
必须配备一个标准、真实且可复现的环境与工具，以便对人工智能能力进行可控比较。该环境应具有现实性，能够衡量智能体在现实世界中的行动能力。同时，环境与工具必须标准化且可复现，从而便于对不同智能体进行可控比较。目前大多数现有基准测试套件缺乏标准化工具，导致智能体开发者不得不使用不同的环境与工具，这使得难以判断性能差异是由更强大的人工智能能力还是其他改进所导致。
尤为重要的是，基准测试套件应提供标准的搜索工具，使其能够在可复现的测试阶段访问相同的文档语料库；然而，大规模优化后的搜索索引成本极高，而公开的搜索工具又无法实现可复现性；目前我们尚未发现任何此类公开、可复现且大规模可用的搜索工具。3. 报告必须考虑混杂变量——尤其是计算成本和工具使用情况。必须计入成本因素，因为即使是简单的策略，如多次重复任务并采用多数投票方式，也能通过节省资金来提高准确性（Kapoor等，2024；2025）。
控制工具使用因素对于区分由模型或智能体架构改进带来的收益与因能够优先访问专业信息源而获得的优势也是至关重要的。

units.en: 4. Task interfaces must be standardized to facilitate integration of general agents. General agents that can perform many different tasks are likely to better meet diverse real-world needs. Unfortunately, most previous benchmark suites require general agent developers to adapt agents for individual tasks, introducing developer bias and hindering development.

Unfortunately, most previous benchmark suites require general agent developers to adapt agents for individual tasks, introducing developer bias and hindering development.
units.zh: 4. 任务接口必须实现标准化，以便实现通用智能体的集成。能够执行多种不同任务的通用智能体更有可能满足各种现实需求。不幸的是，大多数之前的基准测试套件要求通用智能体开发者为特定任务调整智能体，这会导致开发者偏见，并阻碍开发进程。

units.en: To support the development of general agents, task interfaces should provide ‘reasonable’ accommodation for an intelligent agent that has not been developed specifically for the test tasks: complete task instructions, task-required tools, and submission affordances—all in a standard format. 5. Comprehensive agent baselines with standard interfaces are needed to measure state- of-the-art. A large integrated suite of agent baselines must be available to identify which agents are truly state-of-the-art agents and to provide high-quality starting points for future development, yet is lacking from current agent suites resulting in most evaluations comparing only to a small number of other agents or ablations on the evaluator’s own agent.

units.zh:
为了支持通用智能体的发展，任务接口应为尚未为测试任务专门开发的智能体提供“合理”的适配支持：完整的任务说明、任务所需的工具以及提交功能——所有这些都需采用标准格式。5. 需要具有标准接口的全面智能体基准测试，以衡量当前最先进水平。
必须提供一套完整的智能体基准数据集，以识别哪些智能体真正属于最先进的水平，并为未来的开发提供高质量的起点；然而当前的相关智能体套件却缺乏这一资源，导致大多数评估仅与其他少数智能体或评估器自身智能体的仿制方案进行对比。

units.en: B E VALUATION T OOLKIT: O PENNESS AND T OOLING Definitions for the Agent openness and Agent tooling classifications for baseline:
pieces: B E VALUATION T OOLKIT: O PENNESS AND T OOLING Definitions for the Agent openness and Agent tooling classifications for baseline:
units.zh: B E VALUATION T OOLKIT：O PENNESS与工具组件 智能体的开放性定义及基准测试中的智能体工具组件分类

units.en: • Agent openness describes the transparency and reproducibility of an agent’s implementation: – Open-source, open-weight (✓): Both agent code and ML model weights are publicly available, enabling full end-to-end reproducibility. – Open-source, closed-weight (∼): Agent code is available but relies on proprietary ML models, allowing partial reproducibility of the approach. – Closed source & API available (A): Implementation details are proprietary, but the system is accessible via API, enabling result verification but not method reproduction. – Closed & UI only (×): Neither code nor programmatic API access is available. • Agent tooling describes the tool usage and execution environment of an agent during evaluation: – Standard (✓): Uses only predefined tools from the evaluation environment (as defined in Inspect’s state.tools). – Custom interface (∼): Uses custom tools for accessing an equivalent underlying environment, which for AstaBench we define as task-relevant portions of the Asta Environment: * Literature tasks: Information access is limited to date-restricted usage of the Asta Scientific Corpus. * Code tasks: Code execution is limited to an IPython shell in a machine environment initialized with the standard Asta Environment sandbox Dockerfile (or equivalent). – Fully custom (×): Uses tools beyond constraints of Standard or Custom interface.

units.zh:
• 智能体开放性描述了智能体实现的透明度和可复现性：– 开源、开放权重（✓）：智能体代码与机器学习模型权重均公开可用，能够实现完全端到端的可复现性。– 开源、封闭权重（∼）：智能体代码可获取，但依赖专有机器学习模型，只能部分复现该方法。– 闭源且提供API（A）：实现细节为专有信息，但可通过API访问系统，能够验证结果，但无法复现方法。– 封闭且仅支持UI（×）：既无代码访问权限，也无程序化API访问权限。• 智能体工具描述智能体的工具使用及执行环境
评估过程中的智能体表现：– 标准模式（✓）：仅使用评估环境中预定义的工具（如 Inspect 中 state.tools 所定义）。– 自定义界面（∼）：使用自定义工具来访问等效的基础环境，对于 AstaBench 而言，我们将其定义为 Asta 环境中的与任务相关的部分：* 文献任务：信息访问仅限于对 Asta 科学语料库进行日期限制的使用。* 代码任务：代码执行仅限于在已初始化了标准 Asta 环境沙箱 Dockerfile（或等效方案）的机器环境中运行的 IPython shell 中。– 完全自定义模式（×）：使用超出标准或自定义界面限制的工具。

units.en: C S UPPORTING E XPERIMENTAL R ESULTS This section contains supplemental tables and figures for the narrative in Section 5. Table 4 shows the overall results for those agents attempting all benchmarks, as well as agents that can solve all the benchmarks in at least one category. We then show category-specific results, for Literature Understanding (Tables 5 to 7), Code and Execution (Table 8), Data Analysis (Table 9), and End-to- End Discovery (Table 10). For details about referenced agents and models, refer to Tables 3 and 22, respectively. In the Tables, “O” denotes Openness, with values ✓ (Open-source, open-weight), ∼ (Open-source, closed-weight), A (Closed source & API available), and × (Closed & UI only). “T” denotes Tooling, with values ✓ (Standard), ∼ (Custom interface), and × (Fully custom). The openness values apply to the agent (including the model used). “±” denote 95% confidence intervals. Bold denotes the agent is on Pareto-optimal frontier for that column pair. Our results reveal several noteworthy insights.

units.en: D F ULL E XPERIMENTAL R ESULTS Section 5 presented results for the best agents (i.e., agents running with the best underlying model), plus a few additional important data points. Here we show the full set of results for all configurations of agents that were tested (a superset of the results in Section 5). We also show plots of scores vs. costs, including the Pareto frontier (showing the best agent for a given cost). In the Tables, “O” denotes Openness, with values ✓ (Open-source, open-weight), ∼ (Open-source, closed-weight), and × (Closed & UI only). “T” denotes Tooling, with values ✓ (Standard), ∼ (Custom interface), and × (Fully custom). “±” denote 95% confidence intervals.

units.zh: D F 完整的实验结果 第5节展示了最佳智能体的结果（即使用最优基础模型的智能体），以及若干重要的额外数据点。此处我们展示了所有测试过的智能体配置的全部结果集（是第5节结果的超集）。我们还展示了得分与成本关系的图表，包括帕累托前沿图（显示特定成本下的最佳智能体）。在表格中，“O”表示开放性，对应值分别为 ✓（开源、开放权重）、∼（开源、封闭权重）和 ×（仅封闭且包含用户界面）。“T”表示工具支持，对应值分别为 ✓（标准）、∼（自定义界面）和 ×（完全自定义）。“±”表示95%置信区间。

units.en: Statistical Methodology All confidence intervals shown are 95% CIs computed as ±1.96 × SE, where SE is the standard error. For individual benchmarks, standard errors are calculated from the variance across evaluation samples within each task. For category-level qP aggregations, standard errors wi2 · SE2i / wi , where wi P are propagated analytically using weighted averaging: SEcategory = are the task weights (uniform at 1.0 except for the two LitQA tasks which each have weight 0.5). This propagation assumes independence between tasks, which could slightly underestimate uncertainty.

For category-level qP aggregations, standard errors wi2 · SE2i / wi , where wi P are propagated analytically using weighted averaging: SEcategory = are the task weights (uniform at 1.0 except for the two LitQA tasks which each have weight 0.5). units.zh: 统计方法学：所有置信区间均为 95% 置信区间，计算方式为 ±1.96 × SE，其中 SE 为标准误差。对于单个评估基准，标准误差是根据每个任务中各评估样本的方差计算得出的。对于类别级 qP 聚合结果，标准误差为 wi2 · SE2i / wi，其中 wiP 通过加权平均法进行解析性传播：SEcategory 即为任务权重（除两个 LitQA 任务权重为 0.5 外，其余均统一为 1.0）。这种传播假设任务之间相互独立，可能会略微低估不确定性。

units.en: PaperFindingBench PaperFindingBench tests an agent’s ability to handle challenging scien- tific search queries. Given a textual query string, the task is to return a ranked list of papers that satisfy the query. This new benchmark is a subset of our own internal evaluation for our literature-search agent (Asta Paper Finder). Unlike existing paper-finding benchmarks, which are restricted to semantic search queries, our dataset includes metadata and navigational queries along with a diverse mix of semantic queries. The queries are sourced from PaperFinder15 and OpenSciLM16 user logs and the LitSearch (Ajith et al., 2024) and PaSa (He et al., 2025) datasets. Evaluating retrieval tasks is challenging, and our chosen evaluation metrics along with other benchmark details are discussed in appendix E.2. Briefly, navigational and metadata queries are evaluated in terms of F1 over the result set, and semantic queries use the harmonic mean of estimated recall and nDCG. The final evaluation metric is an average of per-query scores.
pieces: PaperFindingBench PaperFindingBench tests an agent’s ability to handle challenging scien- tific search queries. Given a textual query string, the task is to return a ranked list of papers that satisfy the query. This new benchmark is a subset of our own internal evaluation for our literature-search agent (Asta Paper Finder). Unlike existing paper-finding benchmarks, which are restricted to semantic search queries, our dataset includes metadata and navigational queries along with a diverse mix of semantic queries. The queries are sourced from PaperFinder15 and OpenSciLM16 user logs and the LitSearch (Ajith et al., 2024) and PaSa (He et al., 2025) datasets.

Evaluating retrieval tasks is challenging, and our chosen evaluation metrics along with other benchmark details are discussed in appendix E.2. Briefly, navigational and metadata queries are evaluated in terms of F1 over the result set, and semantic queries use the harmonic mean of estimated recall and nDCG. The final evaluation metric is an average of per-query scores.
units.zh:
PaperFindingBench 测试了智能体处理具有挑战性的科学搜索查询的能力。给定一个文本查询字符串，任务就是返回满足该查询的论文排名列表。这一新的基准测试是我们内部文献搜索智能体（Asta Paper Finder）评估体系的子集。与仅限于语义搜索查询的现有论文查找基准不同，我们的数据集包含了元数据查询和导航查询，以及多种类型的语义查询。这些查询来自 PaperFinder15 和 OpenSciLM16 的用户日志，以及 LitSearch（Ajith 等，2024）和 PaSa（He 等，2025）数据集。
评估检索任务具有挑战性，我们选择的评估指标及其他基准测试细节详见附录 E.2。简而言之，导航查询和元数据查询根据结果集的 F1 值进行评估，而语义查询则采用估计召回率和 nDCG 的调和平均值作为评估标准。最终评估指标为各查询得分的平均值。

units.en: LitQA2-FullText/LitQA2-FullText-Search These two benchmarks measure an agent’s abil- ity to answer questions and retrieve papers within the biomedical domain. They are based on the LitQA2 dataset (Skarlinski et al., 2024), which contains 199 multiple-choice questions, each as- sociated with a target paper whose full-text can potentially answer the question. To enable fair comparison for agents using our standard retrieval tools, we filter the original dataset to a subset of 85 questions where the associated relevant paper is available in our Asta Scientific Corpus snippet search index within the specified cutoff date (see Table 2). Following Skarlinski et al. (2024), LitQA2-FullText evaluates in terms of accuracy, the fraction of questions with a correct answer. LitQA2-FullText-Search isolates the retrieval task aimed at finding K papers such that one of them is the target paper for the question, and evaluates on recall@30 (as used in Skarlinski et al. (2024)). To avoid double-counting this benchmark when computing aggregate macro-averaged Liter- ature Understanding scores (compared to other benchmarks in that category), we weight each of these two evals by 0.5 in the macro-average. For additional details and comparisons, see appendix G.2.

LitQA2-FullText/LitQA2-FullText-Search 这两个测试基准用于评估智能体在生物医学领域回答问题和检索论文的能力。它们基于LitQA2数据集（Skarlinski等，2024年），该数据集包含199道选择题，每道题都与一篇目标论文相关，而该论文的全文能够回答相应问题。为了便于使用我们标准检索工具的智能体进行公平比较，我们将原始数据集筛选为85道题目，这些题目对应的相关论文可在指定截止日期内的Asta Scientific Corpus片段搜索索引中找到（见表2）。
根据 Skarlinski 等人的研究（2024年），LitQA2-FullText 通过正确答案问题的比例来评估准确性。LitQA2-FullText-Search 则专注于检索任务，旨在找到K篇论文中恰好有一篇是问题所针对的目标论文，其评估指标为 recall@30（与 Skarlinski 等人的研究（2024年）采用的标准一致）。为了避免在计算综合宏观平均文献理解得分时重复计算该基准测试（相对于该类别中的其他基准测试），我们在宏观平均计算中给这两个评估指标分别赋予0.5的权重。更多细节和比较内容请参见附录G.2。

units.en: ScholarQA-CS2 The ScholarQA-CS2 benchmark tests an agent’s ability to answer long-form scientific questions. Given a complex scientific question like “How is diversity typically evaluated in recommendation systems?” the task is to identify relevant prior work and compose a long-form answer report that appropriately cites sources. ScholarQA-CS2 is a new benchmark that builds upon the recent ScholarQA-CS (Asai et al., 2024) by incorporating real scientific queries and introducing four facets for coverage and precision evaluation of both answers and their attributions, using LLM- as-judge. The average of these four facet scores is the final evaluation metric. For more detail, see appendix E.3.

units.zh: ScholarQA-CS2 该基准测试评估了智能体回答长篇科学问题的能力。面对诸如“推荐系统中如何通常评估多样性？”这样的复杂科学问题时，任务要求识别相关的先前研究，并撰写一份包含适当引用来源的长篇回答报告。ScholarQA-CS2 是一个新的基准测试，它基于最近的 ScholarQA-CS（Asai等人，2024年）进行改进，通过纳入真实的科学查询，并引入四个评估维度来衡量答案及其归属的覆盖率和精确度，同时采用大语言模型作为评判工具。这四个评估维度的得分平均值即为最终评估指标。更多细节请参见附录 E.3。

units.en: ArxivDIGESTables-Clean The ArxivDIGESTables-Clean benchmark tests an agent’s ability to create a literature review table—one whose rows are publications and whose columns consist of aspects used to compare and contrast a set of papers. Given a set of related papers and a caption describing the table’s intent (e.g., “Overview of LLM pretraining benchmarks”), the task is to automatically output a complete literature review table. We release a new benchmark that builds on ArxivDIGESTables, the first high-quality dataset for literature review table generation created by Newman et al. (2024) by extracting review tables from ArXiv papers. Our evaluation includes two key improvements: (i) we curate a small clean subset of instances from the original test set, and (ii) we introduce an end-to-end evaluation methodology for the task. Tables are scored by prompting an LLM to “unroll” them into statements. The evaluation metric is the proportion of ground truth statements from the reference table that are entailed (according to an LLM judge) by the unrolled generated table. For more detail, see appendix E.4.

ArxivDIGESTables-Clean 该基准测试旨在评估智能体生成文献综述表格的能力——该表格的行为出版物，列则包含用于比较和对比一系列论文的要素。给定一组相关论文以及描述表格用途的说明（例如“大语言模型预训练基准概览”），任务要求智能体自动输出完整的文献综述表格。我们发布了一个新的基准测试，该测试基于 ArxivDIGESTables，这是 Newman 等人在 2024 年通过从 ArXiv 论文中提取文献综述表格而创建的首个高质量文献综述表格生成数据集。
我们的评估包含两项关键改进：(i) 我们从原始测试集中挑选了一小部分干净的样本；以及 (ii) 我们为该任务引入了一种端到端的评估方法。通过提示大语言模型将这些表格“展开”成陈述句来对表格进行评分。评估指标为参考表格中真实陈述句被展开生成的表格所包含的比例（由大语言模型评判者判定）。更多细节请参见附录 E.4。

units.en: SUPER-Expert The SUPER-Expert benchmark (Bogin et al., 2024) (Setting UP and Executing tasks from Research repositories) tests the ability of code agents to set up and execute Python machine learning experiments reported in ML and NLP papers. It targets the common yet often non-trivial and time-consuming task of setting up and running code from sparsely documented repositories 15 https://paperfinder.allen.ai/chat 16 https://openscilm.allen.ai/

units.en: accompanying published papers. Given a natural language instruction along with a GitHub repository pointer (e.g., asking to train a model following a paper’s code at a given URL), the task is to clone the repository, install any needed dependencies, configure, run the requested training/evaluation, and report the outcome (e.g., model accuracy). In contrast to other repository-centered code execution tasks, the particular focus here is on low-resource research repositories on GitHub—like those researchers often encounter when validating and expanding upon prior published work. For more detail, see appendix E.5.

units.zh: 与已发表的论文配套执行。当收到自然语言指令以及一个 GitHub 仓库指针时（例如，要求按照某篇论文的代码在指定 URL 处训练模型），任务包括克隆该仓库、安装必要的依赖项、进行配置、运行指定的训练/评估流程，并报告结果（如模型准确率）。与其他以仓库为中心的代码执行任务不同，此处特别关注 GitHub 上资源匮乏的研究仓库——即那些研究人员在验证和扩展已有已发表成果时经常遇到的仓库。更多细节请参见附录 E.5。

units.en: CORE-Bench-Hard− The CORE-Bench-Hard− benchmark (Siegel et al., 2025) tests an agent’s ability to reproduce experiments and analyses from papers. The input is a "capsule" from CodeO- cean.com containing code and data released alongside a published paper, as well as a set of instructions indicating specific analyses to perform with the capsule (full example in appendix H.7.1). The task is to perform these analyses and write answers in a report.json file. The capsules in CORE-Bench- Hard− are chosen to be highly reproducible and span a variety of domains, including computer science, social science, and medicine, and use Python and R programming languages. For more detail, see appendix E.6.

units.zh: CORE-Bench-Hard− CORE-Bench-Hard− 基准测试（Siegel等人，2025年）旨在评估智能体复现论文中实验与分析的能力。输入来自CodeOcean.com的“胶囊”，其中包含与论文一同发布的代码和数据，以及一套指示需使用该胶囊进行特定分析的指令（完整示例见附录H.7.1）。任务要求完成这些分析并在report.json文件中撰写答案。CORE-Bench-Hard−中的胶囊具有高度可复现性，涵盖计算机科学、社会科学和医学等多个领域，且使用Python和R编程语言。更多细节请参见附录E.6。

units.en: DS-1000 The DS-1000 benchmark (Lai et al., 2023) tests the ability of code models on routine data science tasks encountered in everyday research. The input is a coding question and an incomplete code snippet that the agent must fill in to answer the question (see example in appendix H.8.1). The output code snippet is graded by running it against a (problem-specific) test case. This benchmark contains 1000 problems involving 7 Python libraries that were originally collected from StackOverflow and perturbed to avoid training leakage. We use the task implementation provided in Inspect evals (UK AI Safety Institute and Arcadia Impact and Vector Institute, 2025) and report the accuracy of the proposed code passing the target test cases. For more detail, see appendix E.7.

DS-1000 DS-1000 基准测试（Lai等人，2023年）用于评估代码模型在日常研究中所遇到的常规数据科学任务中的能力。输入是一个编程问题以及一个未完成的代码片段，智能体需补全该片段以解答问题（参见附录H.8.1中的示例）。通过将该代码片段与特定问题的测试用例进行运行来对其评分。该基准测试包含1000道题目，涉及7种Python库，这些题目最初来自StackOverflow，并经过处理以避免训练信息泄露。
我们采用了《Inspect evals》（英国人工智能安全研究所、Arcadia Impact及Vector Institute，2025年）中提供的任务实现方案，并报告了所提出代码通过目标测试案例的准确率。更多细节请参见附录 E.7。

units.en: DiscoveryBench The DiscoveryBench (Majumder et al., 2025) benchmark aims to test whether the agent can automatically find and verify hypotheses from given dataset(s), performing data-driven analysis. The input to the task is a discovery goal and a collection of datasets and their respective metadata, and the output is a hypothesis addressing the goal with the highest specificity for the context, variables, and relationship supported by the dataset(s). Optionally, a workflow for deriving a hypothesis can be output to augment information already present in the hypothesis. This is the first comprehensive benchmark to test agents’ or language models’ ability to perform data analysis— including data preparation, basic statistical analysis, complex data transformation, and modeling—on datasets from 6 diverse domains, such as sociology and engineering. We collect task datasets from open public repositories made available by already published works from the 6 domains. The discovery goals are extracted from the associated papers to the datasets, or human-annotated, where each gold output (i.e., the hypothesis) is rigorously verified by data analysis experts. The performance on the benchmark is measured as the alignment of the predicted and gold hypotheses. The final metric, Hypothesis Matching Score, is a product of three LLM-as-judge scores that measure the alignment of the predicted and the gold hypotheses in the dimensions of their context, associated variables, and the relationship among them. For more detail, see appendix E.8.

units.zh:
DiscoveryBench 该 DiscoveryBench 基准测试（Majumder等人，2025年）旨在检验智能体是否能够从给定的数据集中自动发现并验证假设，并进行基于数据的分析。任务的输入是一个发现目标以及一系列数据集及其相关元数据，输出则是一个符合该目标的假设，该假设在上下文、变量和数据集所支持的关系方面具有最高的特异性。可选地，还可以输出一个推导假设的工作流程，以补充假设中已有的信息。
这是首个全面的基准测试，用于评估智能体或大语言模型在6个不同领域的数据集上执行数据分析能力——包括数据准备、基础统计分析、复杂数据转换及建模等——这些领域涵盖社会学和工程学等方向。我们从6个领域的已发表成果所提供的公开公共存储库中收集任务数据集。与数据集相关的发现目标由相关论文提供，或由人类标注得出；其中每个“金标准”输出（即假设）均经过数据分析专家严格验证。该基准测试中的表现指标为预测假设与金标准假设的一致性。
最终指标“假设匹配得分”是由三个作为评判者的大语言模型得分相乘得到的结果，用于衡量预测假设与真实假设在上下文、相关变量及其相互关系方面的契合度。更多细节请参见附录 E.8。

units.en: E2E-Bench The E2E-Bench task aims to test whether agents can perform the full research pipeline of ideation, planning, (software) experiment design, implementation, execution, analysis, and produc- ing a final report, i.e., a complete research cycle. The input to the task is a research question in the domain of AI/NLP and a detailed description of the steps to investigate it, and the output is a technical report, a trace of the agent’s reasoning, and any code or artifacts (e.g., datasets) generated. This is a new release and forms the first agent-neutral benchmark (i.e., a benchmark that isn’t designed to highlight the strengths and scope of a particular agent) designed to compare automatic scientific discovery (ASD) agents. It fills a gap in the current research landscape where there are many such agents, e.g., AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024), AgentLab (Schmidgall et al., 2025), and CodeScientist (Jansen et al., 2025), but no systematic way to compare them. In practice, to allow more controlled system-to-system comparisons, the problems are specified in considerable detail and hence only weakly test the ideation and planning steps. At the same time, these problems are not as prescriptive as typical ML coding problems, e.g., in MLAgentBench (Huang et al., 2024). The problems are created via a mixture of machine generation and human review, and include a detailed task description and a problem-specific evaluation rubric. The final score is an overall LLM-as-judge assessment

units.zh:
E2E-Bench 任务旨在测试智能体是否能够完成从构思、规划、（软件）实验设计、实现、执行、分析到撰写最终报告的全流程研究工作，即一个完整的研究周期。该任务的输入是人工智能/自然语言处理领域的研究问题以及调查该问题的详细步骤描述，输出则包括技术报告、智能体的推理记录，以及生成的任何代码或成果（如数据集）。
这是一次新发布的产品，它构成了首个与智能体无关的基准测试（即一种并非旨在凸显特定智能体优势与能力的基准测试），用于比较自动科学发现智能体。它填补了当前研究领域的空白——虽然存在许多此类智能体，如 AI Scientist（Lu等人，2024）、AgentLab（Schmidgall等人，2025）和 CodeScientist（Jansen等人，2025），但目前缺乏系统化的比较方法。实际上，为了进行更可控的系统间比较，这些问题被详细定义，因此仅对构思与规划步骤进行了有限的测试。
同时，这些问题并不像典型的机器学习编程问题那样具有明确的指导性，例如在 MLAgentBench 项目中（Huang 等，2024）。这些问题是通过机器生成与人工评审相结合的方式创建的，包含详细的任务描述以及针对具体问题的评分标准。最终得分则是基于整体大语言模型作为评判者的评估结果。

units.en: In the rise of LLM-based agentic workflows, the ability to answer challenging scientific search queries, across a wide range of searching criteria, have become possible. However, current paper finding benchmarks largely confine themselves to a small subset of search query kinds (e.g. LitSearch (Ajith et al., 2024), PaSa (He et al., 2025) and LitQA2 dataset (Skarlinski et al., 2024)). They focus on purely semantic criteria, not covering metadata or navigational queries, and they are missing a methodological process to cover the different within-semantic challenging types. PaperFindingBench is a subset of our own internal evaluation for our literature-search agent (Asta Paper Finder), which focuses on challenging queries (the internal evaluation also mixes in a bunch of easier queries, to ensure stability as a product and avoid regressions). PaperFindingBench is designed to be challenging (including things that our system currently does not perform well on) and realistic (based to the extent possible on real-world queries and information needs). It also aims to be broad and diverse in two axes: first, it covers a broader set of information needs. Unlike existing datasets that focus on semantic queries that search for a set of unknown-to-the-user papers based on description of their content, our benchmark includes also “navigational” queries that seek a single known-to-the-user paper based on a short reference (“the alpha-geometry paper”), and queries that define paper sets based on a wide set of metadata criteria (“acl 2024 papers that cite the transformers paper”). The second axis of diversity is within the semantic-search category, in which we seek to include different types of query challenges. The dataset mixes the different categories, and doesn’t clearly indicate which query belongs to which category (even though a human will very easily tell). This is following our belief that a literature-search agent should be able to handle all these query types, even if by merely routing them to different sub-agents. PaperFindingBench includes 48 navigational queries, 43 metadata queries, and 242 semantic queries. Some of the metadata queries contain (easy) navigational queries as part of their criteria, but there is currently a strict separation between metadata and semantic queries (metadata queries do not involve a semantic component and vice-versa), which may change in future versions.

在基于大语言模型的大语言模型工作流兴起过程中，能够针对多种搜索条件回答具有挑战性的科学搜索问题已成为可能。然而，目前的论文评估基准大多仅涵盖少数几种搜索查询类型（例如 LitSearch (Ajith等，2024)、PaSa (He等，2025) 以及 LitQA2 数据集 (Skarlinski等，2024)）。这些基准仅关注纯语义层面的标准，未包含元数据或导航查询，也缺乏覆盖不同语义内类挑战类型的方法论流程。
PaperFindingBench 是我们内部针对文献搜索智能体（Asta Paper Finder）进行的评估子集，重点针对具有挑战性的查询进行测试（该内部评估还包含大量较简单的查询，以确保产品的稳定性并避免性能退化）。PaperFindingBench 旨在包含具有挑战性且现实性的任务（包括当前系统表现不佳的课题），并且尽可能基于真实世界的查询和信息需求。此外，它在两个维度上力求广泛性和多样性：首先，它涵盖更广泛的信息需求范围。
与那些专注于语义查询、根据内容描述来查找用户未知的论文的现有数据集不同，我们的基准测试还包含“导航式”查询，这些查询基于简短的参考信息来寻找用户已知的单一论文（“alpha-几何学论文”），以及基于多种元数据标准来定义论文集合的查询（“引用了Transformer论文的ACL 2024论文”）。多样性第二维度属于语义搜索类别，我们旨在涵盖不同类型的查询挑战。
该数据集包含了不同的类别，但并未明确说明哪些查询属于哪个类别（尽管人类可以非常容易地判断出来）。这符合我们的信念，即文献搜索智能体应该能够处理所有类型的查询，哪怕只是将它们分配给不同的子智能体即可。PaperFindingBench包含48个导航查询、43个元数据查询和242个语义查询。部分元数据查询在其标准中包含（简单的）导航查询，但目前元数据查询与语义查询之间存在严格的区分（元数据查询不涉及语义成分，反之亦然），未来版本可能会发生变化。

units.en: Dataset Creation The Navigational queries are based on PaperFinder17 usage logs, to include queries that, at least at some point in time, paper-finder failed on. The semantic queries are curated from a mix of sources: PaperFinder usage logs, OpenSciLM18 usage logs, and existing literature-search datasets: LitSearch (Ajith et al., 2024) and PaSa (He et al., 2025). We first identified a subset of queries that were challenging for the PaperFinder system, by looking for queries that returned few or no results identified by the system as “perfectly relevant”, and for which we assessed (for query logs) or know (for the annotated dataset) that relevant papers exist. We then manually inspected a collection of such queries to identify challenge types.19 Finally, we created a set in which all challenge types are represented, while prioritizing queries for which running PaperFinder in an ablation mode with any of its components resulted in fewer perfectly-relevant papers for the ones that we do find. The set contains a mix of queries for which we assume there are many relevant results, and queries for which we assume only a handful of results exist. For numerous queries, assessing the relevance of the paper cannot be done solely based on title and abstract, but requires evidence from the paper’s full text. Metadata queries These were hand-crafted to achieve broad coverage of semantic-scholar API usage, as well as interaction between APIs, as well as challenges that are solvable but not directly supported 17 https://paperfinder.allen.ai/chat 18 https://openscilm.allen.ai/ 19 These include, for example, multiple criteria, complex relations between criteria, use of uncommon terms, use of incorrect jargon, seeking details that are not part of the main claim of the paper, query providing unnecessary or even distracting background information.

数据集构建 导航类查询基于 PaperFinder17 的使用日志，其中包含了在某个时间点 PaperFinder 未能找到相关结果的查询。语义类查询则来自多种来源的混合：PaperFinder 使用日志、OpenSciLM18 使用日志以及现有的文献搜索数据集：LitSearch（Ajith等人，2024年）和 PaSa（He等人，2025年）。我们首先筛选出那些对 PaperFinder 系统具有挑战性的查询子集，即那些系统判定为“完全相关”但返回结果很少或没有结果的查询，并且我们已确认（针对查询日志）或知晓（针对标注数据集）存在相关的论文。
我们随后手动检查了这些查询集合，以识别不同的挑战类型。最后，我们构建了一个包含所有挑战类型的集合，同时优先选择那些在消融实验中使用其某个组件运行 PaperFinder 后，我们发现的相关论文数量较少的查询。该集合中包含了一些我们认为存在大量相关结果的查询，以及一些我们认为仅存在少量相关结果的查询。对于许多查询而言，评估论文的相关性不能仅基于标题和摘要，而需要依据论文全文中的证据。
元数据查询：这些查询是人工设计的，旨在全面覆盖语义学者 API 的使用情况、API 之间的交互关系，以及那些可解决但未被直接支持的挑战。17 https://paperfinder.allen.ai/chat 18 https://openscilm.allen.ai/ 19 例如，这些包括多种标准、标准之间的复杂关系、使用不常见术语、使用错误的行话、寻求不属于论文主要论点内容的细节，以及提供不必要的甚至分散注意力的背景信息。

units.en: Evaluation Evaluating retrieval is challenging, as it ideally requires a gold-set of all relevant documents in the corpus, which is often not known. Such a gold-set is available for the navigational and the metadata queries (each metadata query is internally associated with python code that uses the APIs to solve it completely, and whose results we use as the gold set). For the semantic queries, the full-coverage gold-set does not exist, and we resort to a combination of partial annotation and LLM- based judgement. Each query is associated with a (potentially empty) small-set of known-to-be-good matches, as well as with a weighted set of relevance criteria that should be individually verified by the LLM against evidence from the paper for the paper to be considered a good match. The individual relevance criteria were automatically generated by an LLM based on a (potentially expanded version of) the original query. For a fifth of the queries, the relevance criteria were manually verified and corrected or tweaked. As the tweaks and corrections turned out to be mostly minimal, and as the LLM-based relevance criteria were proved to be highly effective for the queries for which manual annotation for some papers is available, we consider all the relevance criteria as reliable, though they may be further improved in future versions. As we aim to assess retrieval and not the judging-LLM’s ability to handle long-contexts, we don’t provide the paper’s full-text for relevance judgement but rather require each result item to be associated with extracted evidence text (either from the paper itself or from papers citing it), which is then fed to the LLM for relevance judgement.

units.zh:
评估 对检索效果的评估具有挑战性，因为理想情况下需要包含语料库中所有相关文档的“金标准”集合，而这一集合往往无法得知。对于导航查询和元数据查询而言，存在这样的金标准集合（每个元数据查询都对应一段使用 API 完全解决的 Python 代码，其结果被用作金标准集合）；而对于语义查询，则不存在完整的覆盖金标准集合，因此我们采用部分注释与基于大语言模型的判断相结合的方法。
每个查询都对应一组（可能为空）已知合适的匹配项，以及一组加权相关性标准；这些相关性标准需要由大语言模型针对论文中的证据进行逐一验证，才能判定该匹配为合适。这些单独的相关性标准是由大语言模型基于原始查询的（可能扩展后的）版本自动生成的。对于五分之一的查询，相关性标准需要由人工进行验证、修正或调整。
由于调整与修正大多非常有限，且基于大语言模型的相关性标准对于某些有人工标注数据的论文查询来说非常有效，我们认为所有相关性标准都是可靠的，尽管未来版本可能会进一步改进。由于我们的目标是评估检索效果，而非评估大语言模型处理长上下文的能力，因此我们不提供论文的全文用于相关性判断，而是要求每个结果项都与提取的证据文本相关联（该文本可来自论文本身或引用该论文的其他论文），然后将这些文本输入到大语言模型中进行相关性判断。

units.en: Scoring Metrics We use two different scoring metrics. For the navigational and metadata queries, for which the gold-set is known, we use F1 over the result-set to score individual queries. For the semantic queries, which are based on LLM judgement, we can compute precision, but not recall. One potential metric would be simply the number of returned documents that are LLM-judged to be relevant, however, this number is unbounded and harder to integrate with other scores in AstaBench. We thus opted to compute recall over an estimated set size for each query (that is, we divide by an estimated set size and not a definitive one), to bound the numbers between 0 and 1. The estimated set size is determined by running multiple variations of PaperFinder with very lenient threshold, taking the union of the resulting set, and then multiplying it by a factor that ranges from 2 to 10 to estimate an upper bound and allow room for additional papers (smaller initial sets are less reliable and are multiplied by a larger number). Note that in extreme cases, this may result in a recall number larger than 1. We bound this by considering the retrieval-adjusted metric of recall@k where we set k to be the estimated set size (this corresponds to the established recall@R metric, but we compute estimated − recall@estimated). Computing recall@k fulfills two purposes: it bounds the score in 1, and also discourages submission of “junk” results. We balance recall@k not by precision, but by nDCG, as it provides a more relevant signal (favoring ranking relevant documents over irrelevant ones). The combination of nDCG and recall@estimated makes precision mostly redundant. To provide a single score for each individual query, we combine the recall and nDCG numbers using an harmonic mean (F1 over estimated-recall and nDCG). To provide a single unified score for the entire dataset, we average the individual query scores, overall queries regardless of their type.

units.zh:
评分指标 我们使用两种不同的评分指标。对于已知黄金集的导航和元数据查询，我们采用结果集上的 F1 分数来评估每个查询的得分。而对于基于大语言模型判断的语义查询，我们可以计算精确率，但无法计算召回率。一个可能的指标就是被大语言模型判定为相关的返回文档数量，不过该数值是无限的，难以与 AstaBench 中的其他评分指标结合使用。因此，我们选择针对每个查询估计的集大小来计算召回率（即除以一个估算值而非确定的集大小），从而将数值限制在 0 到 1 之间。
估计的集合大小是通过使用非常宽松的阈值运行多种版本的 PaperFinder，取这些结果集合的并集，然后乘以一个介于2到10之间的系数来估算上限，从而为额外的论文留出空间（初始集合较小时可靠性较低，因此乘以更大的系数）。需要注意的是，在极端情况下，这可能导致召回数大于1。我们通过考虑经过检索调整的 recall@k 指标来限制这一情况，其中将k设为估计的集合大小（这对应于已建立的 recall@R 指标，但我们计算的是估计值减去 recall@估计值）。
计算 recall@k 分数具有双重作用：它限制了得分的范围，同时也抑制了“无用”结果的提交。我们并非通过精确度来平衡 recall@k 分数，而是通过 nDCG 来实现，因为 nDCG 能提供更相关的信号（更倾向于对相关文档进行排名而非无关文档）。nDCG 与 estimated-recall 的结合使得精确度变得多余。为了为每个单独查询提供单一分数，我们采用调和平均数（即 estimated-recall 与 nDCG 的 F1 值）将召回率和 nDCG 数值合并起来。为了为整个数据集提供统一的单一分数，我们会对所有查询的分数进行平均，而不考虑它们的类型。

units.en: and many others. Evaluating long-form answers to literature review questions is a challenging problem in natural language processing. Many acceptable long-form answers exist for any given question, and even with a dataset of “gold” answers, it is difficult to define how to score a given answer across the relevant dimensions of quality (coverage, correctness, attribution, etc.). The task is especially challenging in the scientific domain, where assessing an answer requires deep subject- matter expertise and can change over time. Asai et al. (2024) introduced ScholarQABench, which consists of multiple datasets to evaluate scientific QA systems over several dimensions. Only one of its datasets—ScholarQA-CS, which we build on in our work—evaluates answer coverage based on a set of target key ingredients (necessary points to cover in a comprehensive answer, manually annotated in that work) for each question. The authors of ScholarQA-CS identify several limitations of their dataset, including that the annotated key ingredients could be subject to “gaming” because they reflect specific preferences of the two annotators, and that the full evaluation relies on heuristically set weight terms. In our new dataset, we instead collect a diverse set of key ingredients from a variety of candidate system responses, and also develop new LLM-as-judge approaches for answer relevance and improved citation evaluation.
